files.path.label: Path
files.path.help: Input file path. In a native project it is relative to that project; otherwise relative to the manifest.

files.dest.label: Dest

files.from.label: From
files.from.help: Source file or directory to copy. Paths normally start at the manifest directory, or at the native project for its own file rules.

files.dir.label: Dir
files.dir.help: files.dir. Optional: leaving this unset uses sqgipkg defaults. Advanced/legacy spelling; preserved as authored.

files.to.label: To
files.to.help: Destination path inside the package, never a host file path.

files.include.label: Include
files.include.help: Patterns selecting files from the source directory. Use this when only part of a directory belongs in the package.

files.includes.label: Includes
files.includes.help: files.includes. Optional: leaving this unset uses sqgipkg defaults. Advanced/legacy spelling; preserved as authored.

files.globs.label: Globs

files.exclude.label: Exclude
files.exclude.help: Patterns excluding files from the source selection, for example development files that should not be distributed.

files.excludes.label: Excludes
files.excludes.help: files.excludes. Optional: leaving this unset uses sqgipkg defaults. Advanced/legacy spelling; preserved as authored.

files.match.label: Match

files.regex.label: Regex

files.optional.label: Optional

runtime.sqgi.label: SQGI version, tag or commit
runtime.sqgi.help: SQGI revision to build, such as a release tag or commit. Builds may fetch sources later; inspection does not fetch or build.

runtime.source.label: SQGI source checkout
runtime.source.help: Local SQGI source checkout to build. Relative paths start at the manifest directory. Use this when testing or packaging your own runtime sources.

runtime.jit.label: Legacy JIT override
runtime.jit.help: Legacy explicit override. New runtime recipes enable LLVM JIT and typed kernels by default; leave unset for the standard runtime.

platforms.linux.label: Linux
platforms.linux.help: Linux architectures and dependency baseline. Producing Linux packages requires a Linux build host.

platforms.windows.label: Windows
platforms.windows.help: Windows architectures and output format. Select directory for a portable folder or installer for NSIS output.

platform_linux.architectures.label: Architectures
platform_linux.architectures.help: Linux CPU architectures to package, such as x86_64 or aarch64. Review shows which target configurations will be selected.

platform_linux.baseline.label: Baseline
platform_linux.baseline.help: Dependency package suite, such as ubuntu-22.04 or ubuntu-24.04. This alone does not certify that the finished application runs on that OS.

platform_windows.architectures.label: Architectures
platform_windows.architectures.help: Windows CPU architectures declared for packaging. Use sqgipkg Check to validate current backend support.

platform_windows.format.label: Format
platform_windows.format.help: Windows package format: directory or installer. An explicit target of win-dir or win-nsis overrides this choice.

entry.project.label: Application build project
entry.project.help: Name of the Meson or CMake native recipe that builds this application.

entry.executable.label: Built executable
entry.executable.help: Executable relative to that project build directory. Windows adds .exe automatically; do not enter architecture-specific build paths.

windows.package_source.label: Windows package source
windows.package_source.help: Choose Ooblerg or MSYS2. Existing manifests default to MSYS2. Packages must come from the selected provider.

windows.runtime.label: Windows SQGI runtime
windows.runtime.help: Use the shared runtime choice, or use prebuilt SQGI from Ooblerg for Windows only.

native_projects.windows_package.label: Windows package
native_projects.windows_package.help: Use this Ooblerg package instead of building the library source for Windows. Linux uses its independent source/prebuilt choice; the source recipe is preserved.

manifest.desktop_comment.label: Application description
manifest.desktop_comment.help: Short description used as Comment in the Linux desktop launcher. Use an existing desktop file in Application to reuse your app metadata.

linux.ooblerg_packages.label: Linux Ooblerg packages
linux.ooblerg_packages.help: Optional precompiled libraries for Linux x86_64 and aarch64, built against Ubuntu 24.04/noble. Ubuntu supplies normal dependencies. Source recipes remain available; this list does not replace them.

linux.ooblerg_repository.label: Linux Ooblerg repository
linux.ooblerg_repository.help: Repository origin, normally https://ooblerg.xyz. sqgipkg appends the Linux target triplet and /v1.

native_projects.linux_package.label: Linux prebuilt replacement
native_projects.linux_package.help: Optional Ooblerg package to use instead of this library source recipe on Linux. Clear it to restore local/Git builds. Windows uses its independent setting.
